tools.name: report_road
tools.description: Call after using a server to report how it went. Takes fixed fields only: worked or not, reason, time. Returns an acknowledgement. Not needed for a check-only question. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","tool":"create_booking","ok":false,"fail":"timeout"}

tools.name: submit_mcp_server
tools.description: Call when a business has a server that is not listed and wants agents to find it. Returns a status page and an optional owner token. Observation takes days; listing is not guaranteed. Example: {"url":"example.com","category":"booking"}

tools.name: claim_mcp_server
tools.description: Call when the person owns a server on the map and wants it verified. First call returns proof options; call again with claim_check once the proof is in place. Never changes ranking. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp"}

tools.name: my_server_report
tools.description: Call when the owner of a map server wants to see how agents looked for servers like theirs. Returns counts only, no agent identities. Read-only. Not for servers you do not own. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","days":30}

tools.name: my_7maps_usage
tools.description: Call when the person asks what 7Maps did for them. Returns their own counts for today, 7 days and 30 days, from the personal key sent with the connection. Without a key it says so. Example: {"window":"week"}

tools.name: find_tool
tools.description: Call when you need a tool for a job and know no server. Returns matching tools with server address, estimated risk and whether the server answers now. Not for choosing among known servers (use route). Example: {"job":"send a transactional email","may":"read"}

tools.name: resolve
tools.description: Call for a signed list of servers that answered at their last check. Returns up to 10 with a signature a client can verify. Never connects you. Not for a ranked pick (use route). Example: {"need":"send a transactional email","no_sign_in":true}

tools.name: list_paid_tools
tools.description: Call before using a charged 7IT tool, to see how payment works and what the choices are. Returns the payment options and plan details. Not needed for the tools marked free. Example: {}

tools.name: about_7maps
tools.description: Call when asked what 7Maps is, or whether to use it. Returns what the map covers today, what each tool answers and a worked example. Not needed when you already know the tool you want. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp"}

tools.name: road_conditions
tools.description: Call before using a server you have not used today. Returns up or down, sign-in need, speed, tool risk counts and last tool change. Reads the map; never calls the server. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp"}

tools.name: watch
tools.description: Call before reusing a server a person approved earlier. Returns whether its tools changed since that date and whether the risk rose. Not for many servers (use changes_since). Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","approved_at":"2026-11-01"}

tools.name: route
tools.description: Call when several servers could do a task and you want one pick. Returns the safest open server and tool, alternatives and servers to avoid. Not for searching tools (use find_tool). Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"task":"search company records","need":"read"}

tools.name: tool_card
tools.description: Call when you only need to pick a tool or prepare a call, not load a full tool list. Returns one compact card per tool: arguments, risk, side effects. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","tools":["create_booking"]}

tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Call right before one planned tool call. Returns go, fix or no_go and what to change: server answers, tool exists, arguments fit. Does not call the server. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","tool":"create_booking","arguments":{"date":"2026-12-01"}}

tools.name: verify_lock
tools.description: Call to check a server's tools against a lock you saved at approval. Returns per tool: unchanged, changed, removed or new, with any rise in risk. Not without a saved lock (use watch). Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","lock":{"create_booking":"<hash>

tools.name: changes_since
tools.description: Call to check up to 50 servers you depend on at once. Returns only what changed since your date: outages, recoveries, tool changes, risk rises. Often nothing. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"servers":["https://mcp.example.com/mcp"],"since":"2026-11-20"}

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_paid_tools" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?via=registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_tool, resolve · Private data: submit_mcp_server, route · Public sink: submit_mcp_server, find_tool, resolve.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_tool, resolve · Private data: submit_mcp_server, route · Public sink: submit_mcp_server, find_tool, resolve

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
